learning_plan.execution_strategy_summary: Alright, future Backend Engineer! This plan is laser-focused on transforming your academic Computer Science foundation, rich with Node.js, TypeScript, and real-world project experience, into production-ready expertise in just two intense months. We're not just learning; we're building a demonstrable, FAANG-ready backend project from day one, rigorously applying industry best practices, and ensuring you're not just skilled, but strategically positioned for interviews. Your existing familiarity with the stack gives you an incredible head start, allowing us to dive deeper into advanced concepts and practical application immediately, bypassing beginner material entirely.

monthly_plan.theme: Solidifying Core Backend Foundations & Kicking Off Your Capstone
weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: We're immediately leveling up your Node.js and TypeScript. You'll dive into the Event Loop, advanced TS features like generics and decorators, and robust error handling. Your goal is to refactor an existing script into a type-safe, performant CLI tool with logging and comprehensive error management.

Week 2: It's time to build! You'll kick off your 'Project Management API' capstone. This week focuses on mastering REST principles, designing clean resource-oriented APIs with Express.js, and implementing core routes and middleware (like basic validation) for your new system. Think Users, Projects, Tasks.

Week 3: Now we're bringing in the data. You'll design a normalized MySQL schema for your Project Management API and integrate it using a powerful ORM like Prisma. This week is all about implementing CRUD operations, database migrations, and understanding transaction management.

Week 4: We'll wrap up the initial build-out of your API by focusing on complex data interactions. You'll use your ORM for advanced queries (filtering, pagination, sorting) across multiple tables within your Project Management system, ensuring your data layer is robust and performant.
technical_skills_to_master: Production-grade Node.js and TypeScript engineering (Event Loop, advanced types, async patterns, error handling).
Designing and implementing well-structured RESTful APIs with Express.js.
Resource-oriented API design and best practices (HTTP methods, status codes, idempotency).
Robust input validation and sanitization using tools like Zod or Joi.
Designing normalized relational database schemas with MySQL.
Integrating and managing databases with a Node.js API using an ORM (Prisma/TypeORM) for CRUD and complex queries.
interview_prep_goals: Familiarize yourself with common backend system design questions (e.g., 'Design a URL shortener') – no need to solve yet, just understand the scope.
Start a daily 15-minute quick-solve of a LeetCode 'Easy' problem using TypeScript to keep DS&A skills sharp and relevant.
Begin mapping common Node.js/TypeScript interview questions to your learning topics.
what_you_will_build: A robust, type-safe Node.js CLI tool demonstrating advanced TS features and error handling.
The foundational RESTful API for a 'Project Management System' with initial endpoints for Users, Projects, and Tasks.
A normalized MySQL database schema integrated with your API via an ORM, supporting full CRUD operations for your resources.
job_hunt_action_items: Optimize your LinkedIn profile: update your headline and summary to reflect your target role ('Backend Developer | Node.js/TypeScript').

Refine your existing resume: highlight your internship and real-world projects, focusing on *impact* and *technologies* used, especially Node.js, TypeScript, and database skills. Make sure it's ATS-friendly.

curated_resources.recommended_search_term: Official Node.js Documentation Event Loop, Official TypeScript Documentation Advanced Types
Academind Node.js Express.js Tutorial, Official Express.js Documentation
Prisma Documentation Get Started, freeCodeCamp SQL Basics

monthly_plan.milestone_deliverable: A functional 'Project Management API' backend with a MySQL database, supporting core CRUD operations, built with Express.js and TypeScript, and documented with Postman.

monthly_plan.theme: Production Readiness, Deployment, and Interview Mastery
weekly_micro_goals: Week 5: Quality is king. You'll implement comprehensive unit tests for your API's service layer and integration tests for your API endpoints using Jest and Supertest. This builds on academic understanding to production-grade testing, mocking dependencies, and ensuring high test coverage.

Week 6: Security is non-negotiable. This week you'll integrate JWT-based authentication and role-based authorization into your Project Management API. You'll learn about OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, secure password hashing with bcrypt, and set up critical security features like CORS and basic rate limiting.

Week 7: Taking your project to the cloud! You'll containerize your entire Project Management API (Node.js app + MySQL) using Docker and Docker Compose. Then, you'll get hands-on experience deploying this containerized application to a basic AWS EC2 instance, demonstrating fundamental cloud deployment skills.

Week 8: The final push! You'll refine your Capstone project, implement a basic CI/CD pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions for build/test), and add a simple caching layer. This week is heavily weighted towards intense DS&A problem-solving (focusing on 'Medium' LeetCode problems), mock technical interviews, and polishing your entire portfolio for job applications.
technical_skills_to_master: Implementing robust unit and integration tests for backend services and APIs.
Applying Test-Driven Development (TDD) principles to improve code quality.
Designing and implementing secure JWT-based authentication and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
Understanding and mitigating common API security vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10).
Containerizing applications with Docker and orchestrating multi-container setups with Docker Compose.
Deploying applications to cloud environments (AWS EC2/Elastic Beanstalk) and basic monitoring.
Advanced Git commands and collaborative workflows (rebase, cherry-pick, conflict resolution).
Applying efficient Data Structures & Algorithms to solve LeetCode 'Medium' level problems and articulate complexity analysis.
interview_prep_goals: Dedicate daily time to solving 1-2 LeetCode 'Medium' problems, focusing on pattern recognition (e.g., two pointers, sliding window) and complexity analysis.
Prepare for behavioral interviews using the STAR method, linking your project work to common behavioral questions.
Research and practice common System Design questions, using your Capstone project as a reference point for discussion.
what_you_will_build: A fully tested 'Project Management API' with high unit and integration test coverage.
A secured 'Project Management API' featuring JWT authentication, RBAC, password hashing, CORS, and rate limiting.
A Dockerized 'Project Management API' (app + DB) deployable to AWS EC2.
A 'production-ready' Project Management API including a basic CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions) and simple caching.

Tailor your resume and cover letter for specific job postings, using keywords from the job descriptions.

critical_guidelines: **Embrace the 70/30 Rule, Relentlessly:** You're a doer. Spend no more than 30% of your daily hour on reading or watching tutorials. The other 70% is for *active coding, debugging, and project building*. This is how you build muscle memory and true understanding, not just theoretical knowledge.

**Time-Box Your Struggles:** When you hit a bug or a complex problem, give yourself a strict time limit (e.g., 30-45 minutes). If you're stuck, seek help! Ping a friend, search Stack Overflow, or take a break and revisit. Wasting hours on one bug can derail your entire tight schedule.

**Your Capstone is Your Resume:** Forget generic To-Do lists. Your 'Project Management API' is your living, breathing portfolio piece. Every new skill you learn *must* be integrated into it. Make it shine – with tests, security, documentation, and deployment. This is what recruiters want to see.

**Leverage Your Buffer Hours Wisely:** Those 5 buffer hours aren't just for emergencies; they're also for mental breaks or diving slightly deeper into a concept that genuinely excites you and has high hiring impact. Don't feel guilty using them for self-care or focused, unplanned learning.

**DS&A is a Daily Ritual:** Even with a heavy project load, dedicating 15-30 minutes *every single day* to DS&A problems will compound significantly. Focus on patterns and understanding *why* a solution works, not just memorizing syntax.
learning_plan.final_readiness_summary: In just two months, you've transformed! By leveraging your existing Node.js, TypeScript, and real-world experience, you've not only deepened your understanding of backend engineering principles but also built a robust, tested, secure, and deployed Project Management API from scratch. Recruiters won't just see a CSE graduate; they'll see a 'Backend Developer with production experience' who can design, build, test, secure, and deploy a full-stack application, articulate technical decisions, and solve complex problems. You're no longer just familiar with frameworks; you're a builder, a problem-solver, and a truly competitive candidate ready for FAANG-level challenges. Go get 'em!
